title: in-toto-envelope-v1 - Envelope field requirements (generic and DSSE profile), media types, file names
$comment: DERIVED - not verbatim. The source (spec/v1/envelope.md) contains no schema, no code block and no grammar; every constraint here was written by this library from its prose (section numbers are those of the .cache rendering: 1 Schema, 2 Fields, 3 File naming convention, 4 Storage convention, 4.1 Examples). Do not cite this file as the in-toto specification's schema. What each definition cannot bind is listed in its own $comment and in x-open. Checked by check-envelope.derived.py against ../examples/cases.derived.json (accept and reject instances, with a mutation pass proving the keywords bind). JSON Schema validators treat contentEncoding/contentMediaType/contentSchema as annotations; check-envelope.derived.py asserts them.
x-open: encoding of the signature bytes: 'determined by the envelope schema' (section 2); a signature element is unconstrained in GenericEnvelope
whether keyid sits at the top level or inside each signature: section 2 lets the envelope schema nest it (R-0011); both are accepted by GenericEnvelope

keyid typing: the source gives keyid no type. A keyid nested in a signature element (one per signature) is typed as a string, as DSSE v1.0 does; a top-level keyid is left unconstrained, because one per signing key used (section 2, line 34, R-0010) makes a list as natural as a string
DsseSignature members (sig, keyid) are DSSE v1.0 fields defined OUTSIDE this source; sig is typed but not required here because this source says nothing about it

base64 alphabet and padding for payload: the source says 'base64-encoded' only; both RFC 4648 alphabets are accepted and padding is optional, but padding that is present must be what the length calls for (check-envelope.derived.py's content check)

character set of <encoding>, <predicate>, <step-name>, <env-name>: the source defines none (a <predicate> is to match a predicate specification filename without its extension, R-0016 and R-0026, the files lying under ../predicates, outside this source); the pattern RN below is a library assumption
whether an empty signatures array is acceptable: the source requires an array and multi-signature support, never a minimum
unknown top-level members, media-type parameters and letter case of media types: the source is silent

not wire-observable and therefore not bound: that payloadType is signed with the payload, that a verifier must not parse the payload before verifying, canonicalization independence, algorithm hints, consumers' reliance on predicateType

RN.$comment: ASSUMPTION, not source: the character class used inside the media-type and file-name patterns below is [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9!#$&^_.-]* (an RFC 6838 restricted-name without '+', so '+' stays the delimiter before the suffix). Kept as documentation; patterns inline it because $ref cannot be spliced into a regex.

PayloadTypeGeneric.$comment: section 2, lines 39-40 (R-0014): the general form application/vnd.in-toto+<encoding>. NOTE the predicate-specific form of line 45 (application/vnd.in-toto.<predicate>+json, R-0015) does NOT match this form: source defect SD-1 in ../normative.md.

PayloadTypeDsse.$comment: section 2, lines 45-46 (R-0015): one of two values, application/vnd.in-toto.<predicate>+json or application/vnd.in-toto+json. <predicate> is not checked against ../predicates (outside the source).

StorageMediaType.$comment: section 4, lines 78-79 (R-0025): the media type application/vnd.in-toto.<predicate>+dsse, recommended for denoting an individual attestation in a storage system. Names the stored Envelope, never a payloadType; the no-predicate form application/vnd.in-toto+dsse is not given by the source and is rejected (SD-6).

EnvelopeFileName.$comment: section 3, lines 62-74 (R-0021 to R-0024): an Envelope kept alone in a file, not in a Bundle, is recommended the suffix .json; <step-name>.json, <env-name>.json. A file name is a single path segment: no separator, no line break.

EnvelopeFileNameWithKeyid.$comment: section 3, lines 71-74: <step/env-name>.<keyid[0:8]>.json - exactly 8 characters of the truncated KEYID. The character set of a KEYID is defined outside this source (in-toto spec 4.2.1), so no hex is assumed. Every such name also matches EnvelopeFileName and cannot be told from a step name that itself contains a dot (SD-10).

Base64Text.$comment: section 2, line 58 (R-0020): base64-encoded. Alphabet and padding are not stated; both RFC 4648 alphabets accepted and '=' padding optional. The pattern admits 0-2 '='; the content check in check-envelope.derived.py also rejects padding other than what the length calls for, and a string mixing '+/' with '-_'.

Statement.$comment: section 2, lines 46-47 (R-0039): the payload is to be a JSON object whose _type field names its schema. The Statement layer (statement.md) is outside this source; only the presence of _type is bound.

DsseSignature.$comment: OUTSIDE THIS SOURCE: sig and keyid are DSSE v1.0 members; the source only defers to DSSE (line 8) and says keyid may be nested in the signature array (lines 34-35). sig is not required here because nothing in this source requires it.

GenericSignature.$comment: section 2, lines 32-33 (R-0037): signature bytes are encoded as the envelope schema says, so an element is unconstrained, except that when it is an object a nested keyid is typed as a string (lines 34-35, R-0011, permit the nesting; the string type is this schema's assumption, x-open).

GenericEnvelope.$comment: section 2, lines 28-40 (R-0034 and the rules it scopes): general field requirements. Binds the canonical names only; '(or equivalent)' names of other envelope formats are outside what a JSON Schema can say. signatures is REQUIRED (line 31, R-0035); keyid and payload are SHOULD (lines 34 and 36, R-0010 and R-0012), so not required. payloadType has no presence rule: line 38 (R-0013) has it signed and lines 39-40 (R-0014) fix its form. This schema reads it as optional, the form applying when it is present; R-0043 infers that it must be present. Two readings: SD-2. Line 13 (R-0004) is an ITE-5 criterion on a format, not a rule on this field. A top-level keyid is unconstrained (x-open). payload content is unconstrained here: only the DSSE profile says base64 JSON.

keyid.$comment: no type: see x-open, keyid typing

DsseEnvelope.$comment: sections 1-2, lines 8 and 42-58 (R-0001, R-0038 and the rules it scopes): the DSSE profile. payloadType is required here because line 45 (R-0015) says it MUST be set (interpretation: 'set' read as present). payload stays optional, also a reading: line 36 (R-0012) asks only that it be included, and line 58 (R-0020) is read as applying when it is present; DSSE v1.0's own rules, outside this source, are not consulted. The payloadType forms of PayloadTypeDsse are NOT a subset of PayloadTypeGeneric (SD-1).
